- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% to compensate for bearish bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 2–5 day lag correction to avoid immediate overshoot after sentiment spikes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model exhibits mean reversion bias — overestimates in early days, underestimates in late days; apply a smoothing filter (e.g., 3-point moving average) to reduce volatility.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.67), model tends to overforecast; cap forecast at 1.5x historical max for 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model fails to adjust quickly; apply a 1–2 day delay in adjusting forecast upward.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds 5x historical mean, model often underestimates; apply a “high volatility” multiplier (e.g., +20% for >5x mean) if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
